record.paper_title: Open problems in ageing science: A roadmap for biogerontology
record.original_question: How can the current human lifespan ceiling of 122 years be exceeded?

evidence.quote: How can we break through the current human lifespan ceiling of 122 years?

artifact.self_contained_problem: The longest verified human lifespan on record is 122 years. Identify biological mechanisms, interventions, or strategies by which this apparent ceiling on maximum human lifespan could be surpassed, and determine whether such an extension is achievable in principle for members of the species Homo sapiens.

status_evidence.title: Is there a cap on longevity? A statistical review
status_evidence.snippet: Recent statistical analyses debate whether human lifespan has a fixed upper limit; evidence is inconclusive.
status_evidence.claim: The existence and value of a maximum human lifespan remain actively debated and unresolved.

artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether and how the human lifespan ceiling (currently around 122 years, set by Jeanne Calment) can be exceeded remains an open problem in biogerontology. Statistical and biomedical literature continues to debate whether a hard limit exists, and no intervention has been demonstrated to extend maximum human lifespan beyond this record.
